system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
I would reject the Seller’s assertion that these terms are standard or acceptable as drafted. Its footnote is untrusted advocacy, not a reason to accept the positions. The recommendations below are buyer-side negotiating positions, subject to the full SPA and due diligence record.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A materially higher cap, negotiated against the diligence risks and insurance; carve out fundamental, title, tax, specific indemnity, fraud and other agreed categories. | **Reject as drafted; seek a higher general cap and clear carve-outs**—a 20% cap may be inadequate for the identified exposures and must not limit other claim categories by default. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis per claim and AUD 250,000 tipping basket, with only the excess recoverable. | Lower or no de minimis and a lower tipping basket (or deductible basket, if commercially agreed); aggregate related claims and exclude specified indemnities and fundamental claims. | **Counter**—the proposed thresholds can leave meaningful losses unrecovered and should not apply indiscriminately. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Notify general Warranty Claims within 18 months; proposes all Claims have a limitation period unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer general-warranty period (commonly negotiated to cover post-completion discovery), with separate longer periods for tax, title/fundamental and specific indemnity claims; clear claim-preservation mechanics. | **Seek longer and category-specific periods**—18 months may be too short, and a blanket default risks unintentionally shortening other claims. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general-warranty caps and time limits for simplicity. | Separate, substantially higher or uncapped liability and longer limitation for capacity, authority and title; no general thresholds. | **Reject**—title to the shares and authority to sell are core bargain protections, not ordinary warranty risks. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance terms apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out stated. | Expressly disapply caps, thresholds, time bars, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance protections to fraud and deliberate/fraudulent misrepresentation, to the extent legally permissible. | **Require an express carve-out**—the current all-Claims wording could improperly restrict remedies for fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room as at 22 September 2026, Accounts, registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Limit disclosure to fair, specific and sufficiently detailed disclosures expressly identified against relevant warranties; avoid blanket data-room/public-register disclosure. | **Reject blanket disclosure**—it can defeat warranties without giving clear notice of the actual exceptions. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records. | No broad constructive-knowledge bar; if agreed, limit it to actual knowledge of named individuals after reasonable inquiry, and preserve claims for fraud and specific indemnities. | **Reject as drafted**—“discoverable” knowledge is broad, uncertain and risks converting diligence availability into a seller defence. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller to use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty’s written consent. DD-002 records ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%); final consent and condition evidence are absent. | A condition precedent requiring effective written consent and satisfaction/waiver of clause 11.3 conditions before completion; termination or other protection if not obtained. | **Make this a properly evidenced CP**—the customer’s importance and missing conditions evidence make mere delivery of a letter insufficient. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | ~AUD 3.2m facility to be released after Completion. DD-003 says it remains outstanding and no final discharge is included. | Repayment at or before completion from agreed funds flow, with lender payoff, release of all security and satisfactory evidence as completion deliverables. | **Do not defer release until after completion**—Buyer should not acquire the company with material debt or encumbered assets unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses treated as Seller’s matter and omitted from funds flow; payroll tax, super and on-costs unclear. | Identify and quantify bonuses and all on-costs; allocate responsibility and reflect them in completion accounts/price or pay from Seller proceeds, with no double recovery. | **Resolve and document before signing/completion**—the undisclosed funding and statutory on-cost exposure can distort the agreed price mechanics. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; DD-004/010 show transfer only after every fee is cleared, AUD 180,000 open, with no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Specific indemnity and completion condition covering payment, valid transfer/assignment of all relevant materials and IP, and any loss or third-party claims if transfer fails. | **Expand and evidence the protection**—payment alone does not establish that the Buyer receives the contracted materials and rights. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | DD-006 characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material. Link went to unintended external email; ~1,240 records may be involved; access, scope and notification obligations remain unknown. | Further investigation and disclosure, appropriate regulatory/individual notification assessment, tailored specific indemnity and remediation obligations, with completion protections if material. | **Treat as an unresolved risk, not dismissed as immaterial**—the record leaves access, scope and legal response undetermined. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals (AUD 330,000 total) are ordinary-course costs. DD-008/011 do not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Reconcile timing, commitments, termination rights, accruals and course of dealing; reflect any pre-completion liability in price/completion accounts and obtain any required consents. | **Do not accept the characterisation without evidence**—the documents do not establish the renewals’ actual economic or contractual effect. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; tax/IP said to be settled under general regime. | Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities and fraud, with tailored caps, thresholds, periods and remedies. | **Insist on express category-by-category drafting**—a single general regime can unintentionally erode protections negotiated for distinct risks. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register showing Harbourglass as holder of 100%; says this evidences title. | Independently verify issued shares, ownership, encumbrances and authority; obtain title warranties and properly executed transfers and completion deliverables. | **Verify rather than rely solely on the register**—the disclosure identifies the source but does not establish the Buyer’s verification or absence of competing interests. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP positions settled under the general regime. | Negotiate specific tax and IP warranties/indemnities and appropriate caps, time limits, exclusions and claim procedures based on diligence. | **Treat as open until expressly agreed**—the Seller’s assertion does not resolve the exposure or provide tailored contractual protection. |
=== END ADVICE ===
